description: Pane-state rules for the odin-say sender, as data. Ingested from a field team's pane-rules export (2026-10-31) and reduced to the literal rules this sender applies; every literal and incident below comes from that file. Screens are the last 14 lines of a pane read.
busy_region_note: A busy word only marks a pane busy on a LIVE line: one that also carries a spinner glyph or a status marker, or one of the last 3 non-empty lines. Leftover scrollback text (for example an old 'Thinking:' line above an idle prompt) never makes a pane busy; that false refusal was a field defect (1,485 of 2,451 proof lines in one team's log).

capped.note: A seat is capped when its newest output block (above the input bar and footer chrome) carries a provider cap marker and no later turn output follows it. A cap line followed by a later response is stale and does not count. Nothing is typed into a capped seat; it is reported and refused.

harness_note: Per-harness identity and mid-turn policy. Detection markers are literal footer/chrome strings; the first harness (in table order) whose markers appear on the pane tail is the pane's harness. mid_turn controls what a busy pane means: queue = the harness buffers text typed mid-turn and delivers it as a queued steer, so send immediately and require queue_evidence on the read-back; refuse = the harness may not buffer, so keep the bounded wait and refuse if it is still busy. queue_evidence_placement says where the evidence must appear: same_line (the sent text and the marker on one line, pi) or later_line (the sent text on a prompt line and the marker on a LATER line, claude-code, captured 2026-11-10). claude-code and pi ship as queue on captured evidence; every other harness refuses until its own capture proves buffering.

queue_evidence: Option+Up to edit all queued messages
Press up to edit queued messages

input_bar_note: Only the LAST prompt-glyph line is the input bar; an earlier line with the same glyph is the harness echo of an already-submitted message.
answered_note: A response line (starting with a filled bullet) or a fresh empty prompt after the echoed text proves the message went in.
